In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the power loss of the SiC-based isolated bidirectional dc-dc converter is dominated by the conduction and the switching losses of the SiC modules.
this converter is capable of delivering a power of 100 kW with a maximum conversion efficiency of 98.7%.

the 98.7%-efficient 100-kW bidirectional isolated dc-dc converter has a power-loss breakdown that is consistent with the expectations of the converter topology and that the concomitant switching and conduction losses are about 60% and 40% of the overall losses, respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a 750-V SiC-MOS/ SBD dual-module dc-dc converter is a very efficient power conversion system for high-power dc-dc applications.
the power loss of a high-power SiC-based converter can be reduced to less than 1% per kW at 20-kHz switching frequency, which is comparable with the state-of-the-art Si IGBT-based converters.
a SiC-MOS/SBD module is a promising candidate for a 20-kHz 100-kW bidirectional isolated dc-dc converter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the conduction and/or switching loss reduction of the SiC modules is the most important issue to achieve a higher conversion efficiency in a high-power bidirectional dc–dc converter.
the power-loss breakdown is an important and necessary step to accurately evaluate the performance and efficiency of high-power high-frequency dc-dc converters.
the conduction and/or switching losses can be reduced by using the SiC modules in the dc-dc converter.
